types.research proposal: A worked-out plan: objectives plus intended methodology (and often evaluation), submitted for critique and refinement — a planned research project. Choose when the input already says both WHAT will be done and HOW.
types.research idea: A sketched mechanism, method, model, or construction the submitter proposes but has not worked out (e.g. 'message passing where nodes are Gaussian distributions and edges are Bernoulli variables'). Choose when a concrete technical 'what if we build it like this' is on the table without a full plan.
types.hypothesis: A single declarative, testable claim the submitter wants validated or refuted (e.g. 'attention layers implicitly perform kernel regression'). Choose when the input asserts something checkable rather than asking or proposing.
types.research question: A specific interrogative that an investigation could answer (e.g. 'Can KNN graph construction be made differentiable?'). Choose when the input asks whether/how/why something holds or can be done, without proposing the mechanism itself.
types.open problem: A challenge the field already recognizes as unsolved — the problem statement is established, the solution is missing (e.g. 'scalable exact inference in dense graphical models'). Choose when the input names a known standing problem rather than a new personal question or idea.
types.research goal: A target capability or outcome the submitter wants achieved, stated as an aim rather than a question or mechanism (e.g. 'a model that generates novel molecules conditioned on a target property'). Choose when the input says WHAT should be achieved but neither asks whether it is possible (that is a research question) nor proposes HOW (that is a research idea).
types.gap-bridging research topic: A topic whose whole point is connecting two fields, methods, or communities — the bridge itself is the contribution (e.g. 'bring optimal transport tools to single-cell trajectory inference'). Choose when the input names the two sides but no concrete mechanism; if a mechanism is sketched, it is a research idea instead.
types.exploratory research topic: A broad area or direction to map and understand, with no specific claim, question, or mechanism yet (e.g. 'uncertainty in graph learning'). Choose only when nothing sharper fits — no claim (hypothesis), no question, no proposed mechanism (research idea), and no explicit two-field bridge (gap-bridging). This is the broadest, least-specified category.
